$meta.provenance_warning: The authoritative source — 'startsaudi brand guidelines.pdf' (Drive id 1mbj4j30JoA5iQ1nY0I02KIVzxKVZsCSP, 76 MB) — could NOT be read in this session. Google Drive returned an empty text layer for it (it is a flattened, image-only export) and direct download of the bytes is blocked by this environment's egress policy. Every colour below was therefore measured by pixel-sampling the official web-ready PNG assets in brand/assets/, which are themselves exports from the identity system. Values are exact reproductions of what is in those files, but they have NOT been reconciled against the guidelines document. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q1.

confidence.measured: Exact hex read from an official brand asset. High confidence in the value, unverified against the guidelines PDF.
confidence.derived: Not present in any source. Constructed for build use. Must be confirmed or replaced.

navy.source: brand/assets/favicon.png (icon background, 725,304 px), mark-color.png (wordmark ink, 30,722 px), pattern-navy.png (base field, 790,649 px)
navy.note: The primary dark. Used as page background, icon background and as wordmark ink in the horizontal lockup.

navy-alt.note: DISCREPANCY: the stacked lockup sets the wordmark in #0F172B while the horizontal lockup sets it in #10192A. A 1–2 point difference per channel — almost certainly one file drifted in export rather than two intentional tokens. Standardise on #10192A unless the guidelines say otherwise. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q2.

navy-raised.source: brand/assets/pattern-navy.png (the lighter of the two tones in the pattern, 341,279 px)
navy-raised.note: The pattern is built from exactly two flat tones: #10192A and #14243E, tiling the power-button glyph in a half-drop grid. Reuse #14243E as the raised-surface / card tone on navy backgrounds.

green.source: brand/assets/mark-icon.png — the light end of the mark's gradient; present in every asset
green.note: The single accent colour. On #10192A it carries a contrast ratio of 11.2:1, so it is safe for body-size text and UI on navy.

green-deep.source: brand/assets/mark-icon.png — the dark end of the mark's gradient
green-deep.note: Only ever seen as the origin of the gradient. Against white it is 9.8:1, so it also works as a dark green text colour, but no source shows it used that way.

cream.source: brand/assets/mark-light.png (reversed lockup ink, 34,472 px), mark-icon.png (the power glyph inside the mark)
cream.note: The reversed / on-dark ink. A very slightly green-tinted white, NOT #FFFFFF. Use it anywhere the brand sits on navy.

white.source: Not specified in any asset. The light-background lockups are supplied on transparency, not on a white field.
white.note: Assumed page background for light mode. Confirm whether the light surface should be #FFFFFF or the cream #EBFFF6.

neutral.$note: DERIVED IN FULL. No source available to this session defines a grey ramp. These are interpolations between #10192A and #FFFFFF on the navy hue, provided only so a build has something consistent to reach for. Replace wholesale once the guidelines PDF is read.

semantic.$note: DERIVED IN FULL. No success / warning / danger colours appear in any asset available to this session. A proposal document will need at least a 'positive' and a 'caution' tone for status callouts. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q3.

success.note: Reuse the brand green rather than introduce a second green.

caution.note: Placeholder. Nothing in the identity defines an amber.

danger.note: Placeholder. Nothing in the identity defines a red.

mark.source: Least-squares fit of the green channel against pixel position across the 48,201 gradient pixels of brand/assets/mark-icon.png. Measured axis is 41.3° below the horizontal, running top-left to bottom-right; the darkest 0.5% of pixels average exactly #004D43 and the lightest 0.5% average exactly #27EAA6.
mark.note: This is the brand's one gradient and it belongs to the mark. No source shows it used as a background or behind text.

ink.source: wordmark ink in the light-background lockup

accent.note: The green #27EAA6 fails contrast on white (1.57:1). Use #004D43 for green text on light surfaces and reserve #27EAA6 for fills and the mark.

contrast_checks.$note: Computed in this session with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula. Included so the build does not have to re-derive them.

green_on_white.passes: FAIL — never use the bright green as text on white

inkmuted_on_white.passes: AA (derived colour — AA only, do not use below 16px for long passages)
